title: Evidence & Incident Integration Standard: packaging, access, and retention
author: Lina Zhang
reviewers: Dr. Mateo Rivera, Priya Kapoor, Samir Desai
body:
Overview

This standard defines how evidence required for security incidents, compliance audits, and regulatory requests is collected, packaged, accessed, and retained across Redwood Inference. It unifies RBAC and audit-logging requirements with data residency and secure SDLC hooks so that incident responders, forensics teams, and compliance owners can produce verifiable evidence bundles within SLA windows.

Goals

- Ensure evidence is tamper-evident, auditable, and reproducible.
- Define minimum artifact sets for common incident classes (authz failures, exfiltration, misconfiguration, model-serving incidents).
- Control access to evidence using least-privilege RBAC and just-in-time escalation.
- Reconcile retention requirements across jurisdictions and customer commitments.
- Embed evidence generation points into the SDLC so artifacts are available for automated post-deploy audits.

Scope

Applies to: hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and the control plane components that manage deployments, telemetry, and audit logs. Excluded: third-party SaaS vendor operational logs unless explicitly integrated by contract.

Ownership and Roles

- Security (Evidence Owner): Lina Zhang — final signoff for evidence release.
- Incident Response (IR Lead): owns on-call evidence collection and packaging during incidents.
- Engineering SRE: provides access to runtime logs, snapshots, and rollback artifacts.
- Privacy & Legal: provides jurisdictional retention guidance and approves disclosure.
- Platform Engineering: implements secure hooks (see SDLC Integration) and storage backends.

Artifact taxonomy (minimum set)

For any classified incident, collect the following core artifacts unless explicitly waived by Security/Legal:

1) Authentication and authorization logs:
   - Token issuance logs, token revocation events, OAuth/JWT validation traces, and policy-evaluation decisions (WAF/authorization broker).
2) API request traces:
   - Request/response headers (redact PII), route, model name/version, latency, and error codes.
3) Model-serving runtime telemetry:
   - Sequence length distribution, KV cache hits/misses, quantization profile used, and GPU allocation events.
4) Audit-log bundle snapshot:
   - Immutable audit stream segment (timebox) covering the incident window.
5) Configuration snapshot:
   - Deployed config (feature flags, rollout policy, routing policy) and hash-signed manifest.
6) Evidence manifest (see example): a plain-text manifest listing each artifact path, SHA-256, storage location, and access policy.
7) Chain-of-custody log:
   - Who accessed/packaged the evidence and why (linked to a ticket/incident ID).

RBAC and Access Controls

Principles

- Use role-scoped access with narrow privileges (e.g., ir-lead.read:logs, sre.snapshot:write).
- Default deny for all evidence buckets; access granted by short-lived tokens (JIT) and recorded in audit logs.
- Separation of duties between evidence producers (SRE) and evidence approvers (Security).
- Multi-person approval for cross-border evidence exports (> 1GB or containing regulated PII).

RBAC mapping examples

- role:ir-first-responder -> permissions: incident:read, evidence:collect, evidence:ticket-link
- role:sre-oncall -> permissions: runtime:read, snapshot:create, evidence:upload
- role:legal-analyst -> permissions: evidence:read-redacted
- role:security-auditor -> permissions: evidence:read, chain-of-custody:verify

Just-in-time access flow

1. IR Lead opens evidence request via Incident ticket with justification.
2. System issues a scoped access grant (15 min default, configurable up to 2 hours).
3. All access is logged to the immutable audit stream and correlated with the incident ID.
4. Access extension requires escalation and multi-person approval if outside normal SLOs.

Audit Logging Requirements

Minimum fields for each audit event (schema contract):
- event_id, timestamp (ISO8601), actor_id, actor_role, resource_id, action, outcome, request_id, correlation_id, region, shard_id.
- For authorization decisions include: policy_version, decision_path, policy_evaluation_time_ms.

Retention and partitioning

- Hot store (queryable): 90 days for operational troubleshooting.
- Warm store (indexable, lower-cost): 2 years for internal compliance reviews.
- Cold archive (immutable): per-jurisdiction minimums (see Retention Matrix).

Tamper-evidence

- All audit events are appended to an immutable store (WORM) with periodic Merkle-tree snapshots signed by the KMS key 'audit-root-redwood-v1'.

Data Residency & Retention Matrix

Jurisdiction mapping:
- US: Hot 90 days, Warm 24 months, Cold 7 years — follows internal baseline.
- EU: Hot 90 days, Warm 24 months, Cold 7 years — GDPR: identify PII and retain only if justified.
- APAC: Hot 90 days, Warm 12 months, Cold 5 years — local law may require longer for specific countries.
- Customer-specific: follow contracted retention.

Note: All archives must be tagged with residency attributes and stored in region-specific buckets when the incident involves that residency.

Secure SDLC integration points

1. Build time: produce signed artifact manifest including codehash, dependency SBOM, and build env.
2. Deployment pipeline: snapshot deployed configuration and route it to evidence staging unless flag skip_evidence_snapshot=true.
3. Post-deploy smoke: automatically capture a 24-hour rolling telemetry snapshot for new model variants for first 72 hours.
4. Pre-release security gating: ensure evidence export paths are registered and tested as part of the release checklist.

Incident evidence collection workflow (standard)

1. Triage (0-15 min): classify incident (authz, data-exfil, model-degradation), assign incident ID, and apply evidence-preservation hold.
2. Preserve (15-60 min): take immutable snapshots of audit log windows, lock affected config, and take a runtime memory snapshot if required.
3. Collect (1-4 hours): collect artifacts (see taxonomy), compute SHA-256 hashes, and write the evidence manifest.
4. Package (4-8 hours): encrypt the bundle with envelope encryption using KMS key evidence-enc-redwood-v2, and upload to the restricted evidence bucket (s3://evidence-restricted/{incident-id}/).
5. Verify (8-12 hours): Security reviews package, verifies hashes and chain-of-custody, and records approval in the incident timeline.
6. Release / Legal Review (as needed): Legal may request redaction or region-specific handling before external disclosure.

SLA targets for evidence delivery

- Internal evidence-ready for forensic review: within 12 hours for critical incidents, 48 hours for high, 7 days for medium/low.
- Immutable audit segment snapshot availability: within 30 minutes of preservation hold.

Packaging & Encryption rules

- All evidence bundles MUST be envelope-encrypted with a KMS key scoped to the owning team.
- For cross-border transfers a separate export KMS key is used and multi-sign approvals required.
- Use AES-256-GCM for symmetric wrapping and store ephemeral wrapping keys in the KMS.

Evidence release and exception handling

- Routine internal reviews: Security may release evidence to Legal and Product for investigation. Externally facing disclosures require Legal signoff and redaction.
- Exceptions (e.g., customer-specific data retention or third-party constraints): raise an evidence-exception via the Governance board; record in the Authorization Exceptions register using the company template.

Forensic tooling and CLI examples

- Pull an audit segment (30-min window):
  rwd-audit fetch --start 2026-11-10T14:00:00Z --end 2026-11-10T14:30:00Z --incident INC-2026-2143 --out ./audit-segment.ndjson
- Create a runtime snapshot (GPU state + container snapshot):
  rwd-runtime snapshot create --cluster cluster-prod-1 --selector "app=model-serving" --incident INC-2026-2143 --out s3://evidence-restricted/INC-2026-2143/runtime-snapshot.tgz

Verification and auditability

- Each evidence bundle must include: artifact checksums, manifest, and a signed approval record.
- Security rotates KMS keys per the Key Management Standard and publishes rotation events to the audit stream.
- Periodic table-top exercises (quarterly) require that the Evidence Owner can reconstruct any archived bundle within 72 hours.

Training and exercises

- IR runs quarterly evidence-packaging drills: produce a full package for a simulated model-exfiltration incident.
- Platform teams are required to complete an annual module on SDLC evidence hooks.

Appendix: Quick checklist (incident start to package)

- Assign incident ID and apply evidence hold
- Create scoped JIT access for collectors
- Snapshot audit logs and runtime state
- Collect config, policy, and deployment artifacts
- Upload to restricted bucket and compute SHA-256
- Encrypt with evidence KMS and publish manifest
- Security verifies hashes and signs chain-of-custody
- Legal reviews if external disclosure required
